subject: Subprocessor census and EU routing annotations request
messages:
From: Ethan Riley <ethan.riley@acmetech.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmetech.com>
Cc: Lina Vargas <lina.vargas@acmetech.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Subprocessor inventory and EU routing details needed

Hi Sofia,

We're preparing our vendor due diligence ahead of our contract renewal and need a canonical list of Redwood's subprocessors that may touch or transit EU resident data for the last 12 months. Specifically can you provide:

- A single CSV listing each subprocessor, role (telemetry, caching, KMS, analytics, CDN, etc.), and the country or countries where processing occurs.
- Any DPA addenda or export control notes that reference cross-border flows involving the EU.
- An annotated diagram (or short note) showing typical routing for EU-origin requests and any onshore fallback options.
- Confirmation whether any processor holds customer-managed keys or long-term backups outside the EU.

We appreciate an initial response by EOD 2028-07-15 so our legal and security teams can start mapping. If you prefer, a short call early next week works too.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Riley
Vendor Security, Acme Tech
[e: ethan.riley@acmetech.com]

Thanks — got it. I'll assemble a canonical census and an annotated routing note. I'll need to loop in Legal and Product infra for details on KMS and backup residency.

- Kimberly (Legal) will confirm which DPA addenda are applicable; Marissa (Infra) will confirm routing + onshore fallback options.

If you need the info sooner, let me know and I'll prioritise.

Best,

Subject: RE: Subprocessor inventory and EU routing details needed — canonical packet attached

Hi Ethan / Acme team,

Thanks for the clear ask. Please find our canonical packet attached and a short summary below. If anything needs more granularity we can follow up with per-vendor artifacts.

Attachments included:
- redwood_subprocessor_census_20280708.csv (CSV): canonical list with role, processing country(s), routing notes, DPA boolean, and KMS flag.
- eu-routing-annotated-diagram.png (PNG): simplified routing for EU-origin requests and onshore fallback paths.
- redwood-dpa-addendum-summary.pdf (PDF): list of DPA addenda that apply to subprocessors that may access EU data; includes DocuSign links where required.

Key summary (high-level):
- Total subprocessors in scope: 28 (see CSV).
- Onshore fallback: we maintain EU-region routing and EU-only ingress for core inference and customer data; several telemetry and analytics vendors route metadata through global collectors but do not persist customer content (flagged in CSV).
- Keys/backups: three support vendors have snapshot backups outside EU for operational reasons; those are indicated in the KMS/backup column with mitigation notes (encryption at rest, limited retention, contractual safeguards).
- DPA addenda: we included applicable addenda references and the HubSpot record linking to the contract (link below). Some addenda require a counterparty signature — we noted those rows.

Related links:
- Canonical census (Drive): https://drive.google.com/redwood/subprocessor-census-20280708
- HubSpot deal record: https://hubspot.com/deal/HS-38492
- DocuSign summary: https://app.docusign.com/documents/DS-7721

Next steps:
- If you want us to produce per-vendor evidence packets (SOC/ISO snapshots) for the flagged vendors, let us know which vendors you want prioritized and we'll produce an evidence bundle within 7 business days.
- Happy to jump on a 30-min technical call to walk through the annotated diagram.

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
